hypothesis: Restoring the heuristically B-like memory to its end-of-B parameters will recover final B recall if later memory drift contributes to forgetting.
selection: At the end of B choose the slot with larger mean P(1|x) for x in {0,1}; ties choose slot 0.
intervention: After A returns, restore exactly one selected or other transition table from the saved end-of-B checkpoint; reset beliefs identically before frozen probes. Sham leaves both tables unchanged.
limitations: Post-hoc hypothesis. Direct restoration uses a privileged checkpoint and is not a deployable online learning method. The slot heuristic exploits these high-P(1) B rules and does not apply generally. Task rules are public.
